Operating inflection at a trough valuation; upgrade to Overweight

We upgrade Lufax to OW from N following its 2Q26 operational update, as improving loan growth and leading asset quality indicators provide a clearer path to recovery from a distressed valuation. Lufax also appears relatively resilient to further loan pricing regulation, given its below-peer IRR. At a 0.1x forward P/B and with market capitalization equivalent to only 37% of end-FY25 cash, the current valuation underappreciates the operating recovery and balance sheet optionality, in our view. The interim results in August could be a catalyst through improved earnings visibility, while any shareholder return initiative would represent additional upside from our base case.

- Upgrade to OW as fundamentals turn at a trough valuation. New loan growth recovered to 4.6% y/y in 2Q26 from a 14.8% decline in 1Q26, while the contraction in outstanding loans moderated to 3% q/q. Leading asset quality indicators also improved, with C-M3 declining 20bps q/q, to 1.0%, D30 falling 30bps, to 5.8%, and the consumer finance NPL ratio edging down 10bps, to 1.3%. At only a 0.1x forward P/B, the current valuation underappreciates the emerging fundamental recovery, in our view.

- Lower loan pricing provides relative regulatory resilience. IRR-cap uncertainty remains the principal sector overhang. However, Lufax's blended new loan IRR was only 18.6% in 2025 vs. ~21.8% for peers on average, while its consumer finance loan IRR was 17.2%, well below the 20% cap. We therefore expect less pricing and margin pressure for Lufax than for higher-IRR peers if regulation tightens further.

- Interim results could improve earnings visibility; capital returns offer upside optionality. The 1H26 results in August should provide better P&L visibility following the operational recovery. Lufax's market capitalization is only

of end-FY25 cash, while it generated positive operating cash flow in 2024-25. We do not assume a special dividend or buyback in our base case, but any clearer capital management commitments along with interim results would provide additional re-rating potential.

- Lower estimates, but improving risk/reward supports the upgrade. We lower our FY26/27/28 new loan forecasts by 6% and total operating income by 2%/4%/5%, partly offset by lower operating expenses and impairment charges; our NPAT forecasts decline by only 1%/3%/1%. We roll forward our PT valuation date to end-2027 and revise down our PT to US$2.00.

- Management turnover remains a watch point. The resignation of the CFO and three non-executive directors adds uncertainty to Lufax's governance and internal control reset, but the improving operating trajectory and distressed valuation provide sufficient compensation for this risk, in our view, while the appointment of an independent director with extensive risk management and internal control experience is directionally positive.

spans.content: Upgrade Lufax to Overweight: Growth and asset quality turn at trough valuation

- Distressed valuation despite an emerging fundamental recovery. Lufax trades at only a 0.1x forward P/B, close to its historical low (Figure 1), while the operating trajectory is improving. New loans returned to 4.6% y/y growth in 2Q26 vs. a 14.8% decline in 1Q26 and flat y/y in FY25, while the contraction in outstanding loans moderated sequentially (Figure 2). Asset quality also showed signs of turning: The leading indicator C-M3 flow rate declined 20bps q/q, to 1.0%, the 30-day delinquency rate improved 30bps, to 5.8%, and the consumer finance NPL ratio fell 10bps, to 1.3%. While near-term ROE remains subdued, we believe the inflection in volumes and asset quality reduces downside risk to the earnings trajectory and supports a re-rating from the current trough multiple.

- Lower loan pricing provides greater resilience against potential further regulatory tightening. IRR-cap uncertainty remains the sector's key regulatory overhang, particularly whether the 4x LPR cap, currently applied to micro-lenders, could ultimately be extended to other funding providers. This concern was reinforced by a recent industry self-disciplinary meeting in June (link) that highlighted that overall pricing remains relatively high and requested major platforms to provide data for a sector-wide baseline assessment and a dedicated report to financial regulators. While this does not represent a new pricing rule, we believe the information-gathering exercise could lay the groundwork for future pricing guidance or a broader loan facilitation rate cap. Against this backdrop, we believe Lufax is better positioned than peers: Its blended new loan IRR was only 18.6% in 2025 vs. ~21.8% for peers on average (Table 1), while its consumer finance loan IRR was 17.2%, well below the current 20% cap. Lufax should therefore face less pricing and margin pressure than higher-IRR platforms if loan rate regulation tightens further.

- Next catalyst in August from interim results, which could improve earnings visibility and offer shareholder return optionality. We expect Lufax to release its 1H26 interim report in August. Unlike the 1Q26 and 2Q26 operational updates, the interim results should provide key P&L information and greater clarity on profitability following the near-completion of the full-guarantee transition. This could help validate whether the recovery in loan growth, asset quality and take rate is translating into improved earnings. Lufax's balance sheet provides additional upside optionality: The current market capitalization is only around

of end-FY25 cash, while the company generated positive operating cash flow in both 2024 and 2025. While we do not assume a capital return announcement in our base case, any dividend, buyback or clearer capital management commitment would represent additional upside and could accelerate a re-rating from the current distressed valuation, in our view. of net profit, although it paid no FY25 dividend because of the reported loss.

Investment Thesis, Valuation and Risks
Lufax Holding Ltd (Overweight; Price Target: $2.00)
Investment Thesis

Lufax is a leading technology-enabled platform focused on retail and SME financing. We upgrade Lufax to Overweight from Neutral, as its 2Q26 update showed an emerging fundamental recovery, with new loan growth returning to positive territory and leading asset quality indicators improving. We also believe Lufax is relatively resilient to further regulatory tightening, given its below-peer loan IRR. At a 0.1x forward P/B and with market capitalization equivalent to only 37% of end-FY25 cash, the current valuation underappreciates the improving operating trajectory and substantial balance sheet optionality, in our view. Key risks include further regulatory tightening, slower-than-expected credit-cost normalization, continued management turnover and securities litigation.
Valuation

Our Dec-27 PT of US$2.00 is based on a P/B-ROE model, assuming a cost of equity of 19.8%, a normalized ROE of 7.6% and a terminal date of 31 December 2028. Our valuation is more sensitive to the normalized ROE assumption: a 1ppt increase/decrease in normalized ROE would raise/lower our PT by approximately 39%, while a 1ppt decrease/increase in the cost of equity would raise/lower our PT by approximately 7-8%.
Risks to Rating and Price Target

Downside risks include: (1) further regulatory tightening, particularly expansion of the 4×LPR cap beyond micro-lending to other loan types; (2) higher-than-expected impairment costs under the full-guarantee model; (3) rising competition among online loan facilitators; and (4) adverse developments in the securities fraud litigation, including a larger-than-expected settlement.

Upside catalysts include: (1) higher-than-expected loan growth; (2) higher-than-expected take rates for the credit facilitation business; (3) a better-than-expected macro recovery; and (4) additional shareholder return initiatives.
